item.title: Bomb threats disrupt flights across Europe, no explosive devices found
item.description:
Several Ryanair flights were threatened, including this one, which landed in Spain. FORTA/Reuters Several flights were targeted by bomb threats in Europe on Tuesday. Planes operated by Ryanair, Scandinavian Airlines, and LOT Polish Airlines were affected. No explosives have been reported found on any of the planes. At least seven flights in Europe were targeted by bomb threats on Tuesday. They included two flying to Poland, two to Italy, two to Bulgaria, and one landing in Spain. One of them was diverted, while the other airplanes reached their destinations before being checked for explosives. No people have been reported injured, and no explosives have been reported found on any of the planes. item.title: 'A brighter future' - why Americans came out to vote
item.description:
Voters cast ballots today in US midterm elections that have been shaped by cost-of-living worries, with polls indicating Democrats are well positioned to wrest control of at least one chamber of Congress. Surveys published today pegged US President Donald Trump’s approval rating near record lows , showing voters are particularly dissatisfied with his handling of inflation . Though he is not on the ballot, Trump has been central in the affordability debate: Critics argue his war against Iran and tariffs have stoked inflation, though experts warned who controls Congress will make little difference. “A lot of voters head to the polls Tuesday hoping for a fix for affordability,” The Wall Street Journal’s chief economics commentator wrote. “ They are going to be disappointed .” — Prashant Rao

item.title: King Charles addresses summit as demands for slavery apology grow
item.description:
BEN STANSALL / Ben Stansall/ Reuters King Charles has said Britain’s role in the slave trade “fills my heart with horror and my soul with profound sorrow” in a major speech —but did not offer a formal apology. The monarch has been under pressure to show contrition this week after the U.K. prime minister reignited the debate about a state apology for transatlantic slavery. However, Charles has chosen to empathize rather than apologize during his Caribbean tour. While in Antigua and Barbuda opening the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) on Tuesday, he said: “The transatlantic trade in enslaved persons still casts a shadow over these islands and other members of our Commonwealth. item.title: Trump’s troubles with Iran could open the door to China
item.description:
A federal judge on Monday dismissed the Trump administration's lawsuit seeking to force Harvard University to turn over admissions records as part of an investigation into whether the Ivy League school continues to consider race in its admissions process. U.S. District Judge Myong Joun ruled that the Justice Department had not adequately established that it followed required procedures before suing Harvard to obtain applicant-level admissions data. The dismissal was issued without prejudice, leaving the door open for the administration to file another lawsuit if it addresses the procedural deficiencies identified by the court. "The Government may be able to identify a qualifying determination or cure the procedural deficiency, but it has not supplied a sufficient basis for the judicial relief currently sought," Joun wrote in his 10-page decision.
